This ice, according to him, is several tens of meters thick, and was formed by accretion at the base of the Amery Ice Shelf. The Ross Ice Shelf some distance back from the barrier may also have a sea-ice component at its base, and RISP ice cores will permit the testing of the bottom freezing hypothesis proposed by Zumberge and supported by the observations of Morgan.
Oceanographic Investigations
The Ross Ice Shelf floats above a mass of water whose properties are unknown. Observations along the front of the ice shelf have shown that the deep water of the open Ross Sea is extremely cold and saline. The low temperatures and high salinity of the water on the Ross Sea continental shelf suggest that sea-ice formation plays an important role in their formation. However, the presence of layers within the temperature field of the continental shelf water which are below the sea-water freezing point at one atmosphere pressure suggests that at least a segment of the sea-ice formation responsible for the continental shelf water lies below the Ross Ice Shelf.
A saline variety of Antarctic Bottom Water (AABW) is produced in the Ross Sea and can be traced into the Southeast Pacific Basin and South Indian Basin. A fresher variety of AABW is produced in the Weddell Sea area. The role of the ice shelves in production of continental shelf water and AABW, and their importance relative to sea-surface ice formation are important unanswered questions.
